text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament voted to lower the barrier for parties to enter parliament to three percent from four percent of the vote.
-- Bulgaria's social care minister Ivan Neikov said public employees will be paid weekly to cope with rapidly rising prices. @

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet set up a Financial Stabilisation Council (FSC) which will implement financial stabilisation policy and will negotiate loans with multilateral lenders. The council is headed by Bulgaria's caretaker prime minister Stefan Sofianski.

-- The state National Electricity Company is losing some $2 million daily because of the delayed introduction of a fixed exchange rate regime, the currency board system, and the slump of the lev, energy ministry officials said.
-- An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission is expected to arrive in Bulgaria in the next few days to continue talks on future funding, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet appointed Pirin Atanasov as an executive director of the Mass Privatisation Centre (MPC). The former MPC executive director Kalin Mitrev was appointed as Bulgaria's representative to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in January.
-- Bulgaria's finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski ruled out blocking of deposits in local commercial banks as a stabilisation measure for the country's financial system.

-- Bulgaria's indebted oil refinery Neftohim loans are expected to be rescheduled and the caretaker cabinet is expected to guarantee new loans for the refinery in a bid to end the fuel crisis in the country, prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet sacked the board of directors of the Neftohim oil refinery but did not free former board members from responsibility for the heavy indebtedness of Neftohim which lacks money to pay for crude supplies, the government press centre said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
